newsitem.title: USA: HSN's Internet Shopping Network to launch Web auction.
newsitem.headline: HSN's Internet Shopping Network to launch Web auction.

text.p: HSN Inc.'s Internet Shopping Network (ISN) on Tuesday launched an online auction site on the Web, competing with sites like Onsale Inc. for the dollars of high-tech consumers.
The new site, scheduled to begin auctioning its first items Thursday, is further evidence of HSN Chairman Barry Diller's commitment to electronic commerce, executives said.

Internet Shopping Network Chief Executive Officer Kirk Loevner said the live First Auction site -- located at (http://www.firstauction.com) -- should rake in more than $30 million to $35 million in revenues in its first year of operation.

"Our focus is computers, consumer electronics and general merchandise," said Loevner. Sales will include unique collectible goods as well as sponsored promotions such as a "Great Maui Escape" sweepstakes currently on offer.

First Auction's partners include AT&T Corp.'s AT&T Worldnet Internet access service, Time Warner Inc.'s Pathfinder Web site, the GeoCities Web site and Gannett Cos. Inc.'s newspaper USA Today. ISN currently boasts more than 120,000 members.

ISN has invested more than $2 million in hardware, software and technical expertise in building the site, Loevner said. It is the company's second commerce site alongside (htt://www.isn.com), an electronic store it established in 1994.
The original ISN superstore site recorded more than $11 million in sales in 1996, Loevner told Reuters, adding this figure would "more than double" this year.
Despite the emergence of a new competitor, Onsale's stock rose on the view that this would attract more business to Internet auction sites in the long run.
Stock in Onsale, which went public in mid-April with an initial public offering priced at $6 a share, rose 93.75 cents, or 11 percent, to end at a record high $8.25 on Nasdaq.
Onsale Inc., which mainly sells refurbished and close-out computer and consumer electronics goods, has been one of the first businesses to make money on the Internet.

Last month, Onsale CEO Jerry Kaplan said the company would aim to roughly break even in 1997, after five quarters of profitability, as it invests to extend its brand and build out merchandising capabilities.
Onsale earned $52,000 on record revenues of $12.3 million for the quarter ended March 31. Total gross merchandise sales, including consignments, approached $18 million, it said.
Shares of HSN, the corporate parent of Home Shopping Network Inc., closed off 81.25 cents at $31.4375 on Nasdaq.
